key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphological irregularity need not compromise optoelectronic quality.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a design route toward more durable perovskite photovoltaics by suppressing non-radiative recombination and aging-induced electronic disorder.
method: Form Ruddlesden–Popper capping layers using 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium on 3D perovskites.
Combine statistical AFM with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films show enhanced photoluminescence, more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, and better preservation of optoelectronic homogeneity during accelerated aging than pristine films.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency gains or operational lifetime data, so photovoltaic performance benefits remain to be established.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
